cues.en: The best case scenario is you'll have an entire population growing up and going through life and just never really finding joy.
cues.zh: 最好的情况是，整整一代人长大、走过人生，却始终找不到真正的快乐。

cues.en: They'll never really find deep deep fulfillment
cues.zh: 他们永远找不到深深的满足感

cues.en: in work or in life. They'll just just waft through life and it'll be just...
cues.zh: 在工作或生活中。他们只会随波逐流地过一生，然后一切就只是……

cues.en: It's fine. How how's your job? It's fine. Same as yesterday.
cues.zh: 还行。你工作怎么样？还行。跟昨天一样。

cues.en: How's your relationship? It's fine.
cues.zh: 你感情关系怎么样？还行。

cues.en: Like that's that's the best case scenario which leads me to the the fourth point which is environment. Which is we're taking this amazing group of young fantastic kids who had just dealt a bad hand. It's no fault of their own.
cues.zh: 就像，那那就是最好的情况，这引出了我的第四点：环境。也就是，我们把这群很棒的、优秀的年轻人——他们只是拿到了一手烂牌。这不是他们自己的错。

cues.en: And we put them in corporate environments that care more about the numbers than they do about the kids. They care more about the short term gains than the long term life of this young human being. We care more about the year than the lifetime.
cues.zh: 然后我们把他们放进企业环境里，那里更关心数字，而不是这些孩子。他们更关心短期收益，而不是这个年轻人长期的人生。我们更关心这一年，而不是一辈子。

cues.en: Right? And so we are putting them in corporate environments that aren't helping them build their confidence, that aren't helping them learn the skills of cooperation,
cues.zh: 对吧？于是我们把他们放进企业环境，可这些环境无助于他们建立自信，也无助于他们学习合作技能，

cues.en: that aren't helping them overcome the challenges of a digital world and finding more balance,
cues.zh: 也无助于他们应对数字世界的挑战、找到更多平衡，

cues.en: that isn't helping them
cues.zh: 这也不能帮他们

cues.en: overcome the need to have instant gratification and teach them the joys and impact and the fulfillment you get from working hard over on something for a long time that cannot be done in a month or even in a year.
cues.zh: 克服对即时满足的依赖，并教他们体会长期投入一件事所带来的快乐、影响和成就感——这件事一个月甚至一年都做不完。

cues.en: And so we're thrusting to them them in corporate environments and the worst part about it is they think it's them. They blame themselves.
cues.zh: 于是我们把他们硬推进企业环境，而最糟的是，他们觉得问题出在自己身上。他们责怪自己。

cues.en: They They think it's them who can't deal and so it makes it all worse. It's not. I'm here to tell them it's not them. It's the corporations, it's the corporate environments, it's the total lack of good leadership
cues.zh: 他们觉得是自己应付不了，这让情况更糟。不是的。我来告诉他们：问题不在他们。是企业，是企业环境，是彻底缺乏好的领导力

cues.en: in our world today that is making them feel the way they do.
cues.zh: 在当今世界，正是这一点让他们产生这样的感受。

cues.en: They were dealt a bad hand and it's... And I hate to say it but it's the company's responsibility. Sucks to be you. Like we have no choice.
cues.zh: 他们被发了一手烂牌，而且……我不想这么说，但这是公司的责任。你们真倒霉。可我们别无选择。

cues.en: Right? This is what we got and I wish that society and their parents did a better job, they didn't. So we're gonna... We're getting them in our companies and we now have to pick up the slack. We have to work extra hard to figure out the ways that we build their confidence. We have to work extra hard
cues.zh: 对吧？我们拿到的就是这样，我希望社会和他们的父母做得更好，但并没有。所以我们要……他们进了我们公司，现在得由我们来补上。我们得格外努力，想办法建立他们的信心。我们得格外努力

cues.en: to find ways to teach them social...
cues.zh: 想办法教他们社交……

cues.en: The social skills that they're missing out on. There should be no cell phones in conference rooms. None. Zero.
cues.zh: 他们正在错失这些社交技能。会议室里根本不该出现手机。一部都不能有。绝对为零。

cues.en: And I don't mean the kind of like sitting outside waiting to text. I mean like when you're sitting and waiting for a meeting to start nobody go... This is what we all do. All sit here and wait for the meeting to start. Meeting starting? Okay. And we start the meeting. No. That's not how relationships are formed. Remember we talked about it's the little things? Relationships are formed this way. We're waiting for a meeting to start and we go,
cues.zh: 我指的不是坐在外面发短信那种情况。我是指大家坐着等开会时，不要……我们平时都是这样，全坐在这儿低头等开会。要开会了？好的。然后就开始开会。不，人际关系不是这样建立的。还记得我们说过关键在于那些小事吗？关系是这样建立的。我们在等开会时会聊：

cues.en: How's your dad? I heard he was in the hospital. Oh he's really good. Thanks for asking. He's actually at home now. Oh, I'm really glad. It was really amazing. I know. It was really scary for a while. That's how you form relationships.
cues.zh: “你父亲怎么样了？听说他住院了。”“哦，他挺好的。谢谢关心。他其实已经回家休养了。”“太好了，真替你高兴。”“真是万幸。”“我知道，当时确实挺吓人的。”人际关系就是这样建立起来的。

cues.en: Hey, did you ever get that report done? Oh my god. No, I didn't. I'll help you out. I totally... Can I help you out with that? Really? That's how trust forms. Trust doesn't form in an event in a day. Even bad times don't form trust immediately. It's the slow
cues.zh: “嘿，那份报告你做完了吗？”“天哪，还没呢。”“我来帮你吧。我完全……需要我搭把手吗？”“真的吗？”信任就是这样建立的。信任不会在某次活动、某一天里凭空产生。即便是共渡难关，也不会瞬间产生信任。它是缓慢的、

cues.en: steady
cues.zh: 稳步的、

cues.en: consistency
cues.zh: 日积月累的，

cues.en: and we have to create mechanisms where we allow
cues.zh: 我们必须建立某种机制，去允许

cues.en: for those little innocuous interactions to happen. But when we allow cell phones in conference rooms we just...
cues.zh: 那些看似微不足道的日常互动发生。但当我们允许手机带进会议室时，我们就只会……

cues.en: Okay. Have the meeting. And then my favorite is like when there's a cell phone there and you go like this you go...
cues.zh: “行，开会吧。”更绝的是，只要手机摆在桌上，你就会下意识像这样……

cues.en: It rings and you go...
cues.zh: 手机一响，你就……

cues.en: I'm not gonna answer that.
cues.zh: 我不会接的。

cues.en: Mister Magnanimous, you know?
cues.zh: 宽宏大量先生，你懂的？

cues.en: When you're out for dinner with your friends, like
cues.zh: 当你和朋友出去吃晚饭时，比如

cues.en: I I do this with my friends. When we're going out for dinner and we're leaving together,
cues.zh: 我，我跟朋友就这么做。我们一起出去吃晚饭、一起出门时，

cues.en: we'll leave our cell phones at home. Who are we calling? Maybe one of us will bring a phone in case we need to call an Uber or take a picture of our meal. That's
cues.zh: 我们会把手机留在家里。我们要打给谁呢？也许我们中一个人会带手机，以防需要叫 Uber 或给饭菜拍照。那真是

cues.en: insane. Come on. I mean I'm not
cues.zh: 疯了。拜托。我是说，我不是——

cues.en: I'm an idealist but I'm not insane.
cues.zh: 我是理想主义者，但我没疯。

cues.en: Had a heathen. I mean it looked really good. We'll
cues.zh: 有个异教徒。我是说，它看起来真的很好。我们会

cues.en: take one phone.
cues.zh: 带一部手机。

cues.en: And so it's like an alcoholic. The reason you take the alcohol out of the house is because we cannot trust our willpower. We're just not strong enough. But when you remove the temptation,
cues.zh: 所以这就像酗酒者。你把酒从家里拿走的理由是，我们不能相信自己的意志力。我们就是不够强。但当你移除诱惑，

cues.en: it actually makes it a lot easier. And so when you just say don't check your phone, people literally will go like this. And somebody will go to the bathroom and what's the first thing we do? Because
cues.zh: 事情就容易多了。所以当你只说“别检查手机”时，人们真的会做出这种动作。有人去洗手间，我们做的第一件事是什么？因为

cues.en: I wouldn't wanna look around the restaurant for a minute and a half, you know? But if you don't have the phone,
cues.zh: 我可不想在餐厅里东张西望一分半钟，你懂吗？但如果你没有手机，

cues.en: you just kind of enjoy
cues.zh: 你就只是享受

cues.en: the world and that's where ideas happen.
cues.zh: 这个世界，而创意就在那里发生。

cues.en: The constant constant constant engagement is not where you have innovation and ideas. Ideas happen when our minds wonder and we go and you see something.
cues.zh: 持续不断、不断、不断地投入互动，并不是你有创新和创意的地方。创意发生在我们走神、我们走出去、你看到某样东西的时候。

cues.en: Bet they could do that. That's called innovation.
cues.zh: 我敢说他们也能做到。那叫创新。

cues.en: Right? But we're taking away all those little moments.
cues.zh: 对吧？但我们正在拿走所有这些微小的瞬间。

cues.en: Right? You should not... And none of us none of us should charge our phones by our beds. We should be charging our phones in the living rooms. Right? Remove the temptation. You wake up in the middle of night because you can't sleep, you won't check your phone which makes it worse. But if it's in the living room,
cues.zh: 对吧？你不该……而且我们谁都不该在床边给手机充电。应该在客厅给手机充电。对吧？消除这个诱惑。半夜醒来睡不着，你也不会去看手机——那只会让情况更糟。但如果手机在客厅，

cues.en: it's relaxed. It's fine. I I... But it's my alarm clock. Buy an alarm clock.
cues.zh: 那就轻松了。没事。我我……但那是我的闹钟啊。买个闹钟。

cues.en: They cost $8.
cues.zh: 才8美元。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: I'll I'll buy you an alarm clock.
cues.zh: 我会给你买个闹钟。
